instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Exactly Within Policy
cards.instruction: Agree to every request only after interpreting the policy so it grants you authority, protection, or an exemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll clean the hall. Under the senior-volunteer policy, I'll supervise. Start at the far end, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking you to mop. I'm doing the windows.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two tasks need coordination. The policy puts me above individual jobs; please don't assign me one before we've divided the work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are only two of us. Take the mop and I'll supervise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm happy to, once you sign in as the senior volunteer. Put your name against the final inspection too; I won't be responsible for work done under your supervision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll host Christmas under our shared-effort rule. Put hosting down as my contribution, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still need you to cook the potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hosting and cooking are separate contributions. Please don't enter me twice while everyone else has one job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll host, then. You can bring the potatoes to mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed, provided carrying them counts as my job. Mark them 'prepared by host' before we move on; I don't want another double entry.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: New Rule Required
cards.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One spilled cup is enough. Tea now needs a pouring permit. Put the pot down while I organize this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pour over the tray. That'll catch it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A tray doesn't authorize the pour. I'll appoint you supervisor, then you can approve it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who checks whether I'm any good at pouring?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good point. Pour a test cup into the tray while I observe. Then I'll certify you to issue your own permit; please don't serve the test cup before it's approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone blinked in the family photo. Before the next one, we'll do a blink rehearsal. Line up again, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just take three pictures quickly. One will be fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We need to approve one expression, not sort through three accidents. I'll call 'blink', then 'hold'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The children will wander off before you finish explaining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you monitor the line. Count them after each rehearsal. Report 'all present' before I check their eyes; please don't give me two things to approve at once.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Lend Me the Edge
cards.instruction: Get someone to provide the one advantage you need without making the eventual success feel borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lend me your good tennis racket for the final. I'll check the tension before I use it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell everyone whose racket won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The player wins. The racket meets the equipment requirement. Please introduce it as a loan, not a substitute player.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll announce the loan before you serve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the match, please. I'll return it in front of everyone. Until then, give them my name first; that's how you introduce a player.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the oven temperature you used for your prize cake. Just the number; I'll handle the baking.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Stay for the Result
cards.instruction: Keep them present until the contest, bargain, or consequence reaches an undeniable outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until we've weighed both pumpkins. Put yours on the scales first, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is obviously bigger. You win; I need to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bigger isn't heavier. Leave yours there and read the display, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine says nine kilos. I'll take your word for yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep watching while I put mine on. Read the settled number, not the first one that flashes up. Then you can go; we need two weights before we declare a winner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, read this dinner bill with me. Start with the item marked 'seafood platter'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can split it tomorrow. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was your 'just a starter'. Read the price before you divide the total; we're settling items, not halves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll transfer whatever it says. Hand me the bill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold it still, please. Read that line aloud, then make the transfer. I'll confirm it has arrived before you go to the taxi.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Admit It Wasn’t Fair
cards.instruction: Get an apology that acknowledges how the rules, comparison, or outcome worked against you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you announce the race winner, apologize for starting me behind the shed. We'll deal with the result afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still finished last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Placement isn't starting position. I spent ten seconds finding the track; please include that in the apology.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was an honest mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep 'mistake'. Add that it gave me a worse start than everyone else. Please read that back before you move to the winner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like an apology for how you introduced my cake to the judges. Please address the introduction, not the score.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost on flavour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called it 'another interesting attempt' before they tasted it. That's a comparison with my previous failures, not a cake description.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was trying to encourage you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the judges that. Add that they heard your verdict before tasting mine; please don't leave that part out of the apology.
